subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity requirements & commercial path for HealthSol
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bates <sarah.bates@healthsol.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity requirements & commercial path for HealthSol

Sarah — thanks again for carving out time earlier. Quick note to capture what we heard and the suggested next steps so everyone has the same record.

Call summary (recap):
- Primary pain: unpredictable inference costs and intermittent latency spikes for billing-critical workflows (claims reconciliation batch + near-real-time triage).
- Compliance/isolation ask: strict tenant isolation (VPC + customer-managed ingress), audit logs for model requests, and the ability to run within east/us region.
- Scale profile: start with steady-state ~200 concurrent short-generation QPS (~256 tokens), peak bursts up to ~1.2k QPS for scheduled overnight jobs and marketing spikes.
- Desired SLOs: 99.95% availability with P95 latency < 150ms for 512-token generation on the committed pool; fallbacks acceptable to a lower-cost variant if primary pool is saturated.
- Timeline: procurement window targets signing in Q1 2027; pilot (1–2 weeks) immediately after contract.

Proposed Redwood approach (high level):
1) Dedicated reserved pool: initial commit mapped to 2 x A100-class nodes (NVLink disabled for strict tenant-silo), with autoscale policy to expand to 8 nodes for steady-state growth and burst capacity to spot-backed nodes for non-critical workloads.
2) Network/isolation: private VPC peering + customer-controlled ingress plus encrypted KV and optional HSM-backed key management.
3) Ops & SLOs: per-route latency dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and a canary rollout for model upgrades.

Requested next steps / asks from HealthSol:
- Confirm the QPS distribution above (rough hourly profile or 95th-percentile peak).
- Share the security questionnaire (basic answers in advance help speed procurement).
- Confirm procurement timeline and any PO/contract constraints (term length, cancellation window).

I attached a draft commercial worksheet and our standard security questionnaire for your team to review.

If this aligns, can we schedule a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with your infra/ML ops folks this week or early next so we can validate the NVLink/driver constraints and the burst plan?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0143

Attachments: proposed-quote-hs-dedicated.xlsx (pricing worksheet), healthsol-security-questionnaire.pdf

From: Sarah Bates <sarah.bates@healthsol.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kyle Rhee <kyle.r@healthsol.com>, HealthSol Procurement <procurement@healthsol.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity requirements & commercial path for HealthSol

Thanks Marcus — useful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) QPS profile: the numbers look right for our front-door service. For the overnight jobs, they are batched into 30–60 minute windows; peak burst of 1.2k is conservative. I can export the 95th-percentile request histogram if that helps.
2) Isolation: procurement will require a written statement that the reserved pool will be isolated to our tenancy and that NVLink will not be used to connect our workloads to other customers. Is that something Redwood can commit to in contract language?
3) SLA: the 99.95% availability target is our bar for production; for latency, we can tolerate slightly higher P95 during scheduled batch windows but want the interactive paths to meet the 150ms target.

Procurement timeline: we aim to complete vendor selection and issue a PO between Jan 10–31, 2027. We will likely start with a 12-month committed term and include a 30-day ramp clause.

I'll loop procurement on the security questionnaire separately; I also attached a short vendor intake form we use internally (see: attachment stub below).

Can we tentatively book a technical deep-dive for Wed 11/11 10:00 PT? Kyle (CC) will be the primary technical owner.

Best,
Sarah Bates
Head of Platform Engineering, HealthSol
sarah.bates@healthsol.com

Attachments: HealthSol-vendor-intake-form.docx (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bates <sarah.bates@healthsol.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity requirements & commercial path for HealthSol

Sarah — appreciate the timeline. A few notes from commercial/ops perspective before the technical call: 

- Isolation commitment: we can operationally guarantee a tenant-siloed pool for HealthSol (dedicated VPC + no cross-tenant KV sharing). Contract-level language to explicitly ban NVLink sharing and to require HSM/KMS controls is routine; legal will scope the precise wording but this is standard for our Private/Dedicated customers.
- Suggested starter configuration: 2 x A100-80GB equivalents (committed) + ability to scale to 8 nodes. Preliminary monthly net price (committed): $138k/month for the starter 2-node commit (including reserved capacity discount + base support). Burst capacity pricing and spot options are in the attached worksheet.
- SLA framing: we can commit to 99.95% uptime SLA for the reserved pool; latency SLAs target P95 thresholds per route — we'll propose the interactive route be scoped to the committed nodes while batch routes can be assigned to lower-cost variants with documented fallbacks.

Action items for commercial:
- Marcus: update the quote workbook to reflect a 12-month term with 30-day ramp language and produce a line-item for optional HSM.
- Naomi: start pulling SOC2/ISO artifacts to attach to the procurement package.

Marcus — if Wed 11/11 10:00 PT works we should include our infra lead and the runtime engineer who can talk NVLink/kernel constraints.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Eng Manager, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: proposed-quote-hs-dedicated.xlsx

From: Sarah Bates <sarah.bates@healthsol.com>

Cc: Kyle Rhee <kyle.r@healthsol.com>, HealthSol Procurement <procurement@healthsol.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity requirements & commercial path for HealthSol

Confirmed — Wed 11/11 10:00 PT works for us. Kyle and procurement will join.

I have attached the completed vendor intake form and an initial security questionnaire (we've pre-filled some answers). Procurement asked for an initial estimate to include in the vendor package; Ben, the ballpark you provided is helpful — can we get a short one-page quote summary we can drop into our procurement tool?

Also: procurement has a standard clause requiring a 14-day remediation notice for critical security findings during the contract term. We'll surface exact language in the PO but wanted to call it out early.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Sarah
Sarah Bates
Head of Platform Engineering, HealthSol
sarah.bates@healthsol.com
